mainTopic: Can a woman sell property she inherited before or during her engagement or marriage, and when does her husband get rights to it?
overview: This amud is about property a woman inherits (נכסים שנפלו לה) and when her husband gains rights to it. If she inherited before אירוסין, everyone agrees she may sell it. If she inherited after אירוסין, בית שמאי say she may sell and בית הלל say she may not, but both agree a sale already made stands. If she inherited after נישואין, the husband can take it back from the buyers. The חכמים challenge רבן גמליאל twice: since the husband acquired the woman, shouldn't he acquire her property too? Each time רבן גמליאל refuses to extend the husband's rights to old property. רבי שמעון instead divides property by whether the husband knows about it. The גמרא then asks why the timing of the inheritance matters. It concludes that before אירוסין the property is surely hers, while after אירוסין it is a doubt whose rights it came under. Finally the גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה's report of the חכמים' challenge was aimed at selling from the start or at a sale already made, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Property inherited before engagement: everyone agrees she may sell
steps.stepSummary: If a woman inherited property before אירוסין, בית שמאי and בית הלל agree she may sell it or give it away, and the deal stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who inherited property before she got engaged: בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that she may sell it or give it away, and the deal is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the easiest case. The property came to her while she was completely single, so everyone agrees it is fully hers to sell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before אירוסין no man has any connection to her at all. Even if she gets engaged later, the property she already had stays under her control. This is the starting point for the harder cases that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'fell to her': she received it, usually by inheritance
She becomes betrothed (אירוסין, the first stage of marriage)

phrases.english: A woman to whom property fell
phrases.notes: 'Fell to her' means she got it without working for it, usually through an inheritance.

phrases.english: before she became betrothed
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel agree
that she may sell and give it away, and it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לָהּ נְכָסִים עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְאָרֵס
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property inherited before אירוסין may be sold or given away by the woman, and everyone agrees.

steps.title: Property inherited after engagement: Shammai and Hillel argue
steps.stepSummary: If she inherited after אירוסין, בית שמאי say she may sell it and בית הלל say she may not. Both agree that if she already sold it, the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it came to her after she got engaged, בית שמאי say she may sell it and בית הלל say she may not. Both agree that if she did sell it or give it away, the deal is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the middle stage, when she is engaged but not yet married. Here the two schools argue about whether she should sell in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל say she should not sell at the start, since she is already partly tied to her future husband. Still, the argument is only about what she should do beforehand. Once she has sold, both schools agree the sale holds. The גמרא explains the reason in Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: She sold or gave away, after the fact

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'may she sell?' (לכתחילה, beforehand) with 'is the sale valid?' (בדיעבד, after the fact). בית הלל forbid selling to begin with, yet they still agree the sale stands once it is done.

phrases.english: If it fell to her after she was betrothed
Beit Shammai say: she may sell,
and Beit Hillel say: she may not sell.
Both these and those agree
that if she sold or gave it away, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case before אירוסין to the case after it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property inherited after אירוסין: בית שמאי say she may sell and בית הלל say she may not. Both agree a completed sale is valid.

steps.title: The חכמים challenge רבן גמליאל: he acquired her, so why not her property?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports that the חכמים asked רבן גמליאל: since the man already acquired the woman through אירוסין, he should acquire her property too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: the חכמים said before רבן גמליאל: Since he acquired the woman, should he not acquire the property too?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against letting the woman control property she inherited after אירוסין. Their point is that the man already has her, so he should have her property as well. Step 14 asks exactly which ruling they were attacking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their logic is that if the man's acquisition takes hold on the woman herself, it should also reach her belongings. If that were true, any sale she made after אירוסין should be cancelled.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
The Sages said before Rabban Gamliel:
Since he acquired the woman,
should he not acquire the property?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְזָכָה בָּאִשָּׁה, לֹא יִזְכֶּה בַּנְּכָסִים
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's position that property she inherited after אירוסין stays under the woman's control. Step 14 asks whether the challenge targets selling from the start (בית שמאי) or only whether a completed sale is valid (which בית הלל also accept).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Acquiring the woman should carry with it acquiring her property, so her sale should be cancelled.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: we are already embarrassed about the new property
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers that even the rule about 'new' property is hard to explain, so they should not make the old property harder too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: We are embarrassed about the new property, and you want to pile the old property on us too?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל pushes back. He admits that even the husband's rights over newer property are hard to justify, so he refuses to stretch those rights to older property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'new' property is what she gets after marriage, where the husband does have rights. רבן גמליאל finds even that hard to explain, since it seems to be hers. If the strong rule is already hard to defend, it certainly should not be extended to the 'old' property she already had.

keyTerms.meaning: New: property that came to her later
Ashamed, embarrassed (here: unable to give a good reason)
Old: property she already had earlier

phrases.english: He said to them:
About the new property we are ashamed,
phrases.notes: He means: we cannot fully explain why the husband controls even the property that comes to her after marriage.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאַתֶּם מְגַלְגְּלִין עָלֵינוּ אֶת הַיְּשָׁנִים?!
phrases.english: and yet you roll the old property onto us too?!

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the comparison: the husband's rights are themselves hard to explain, so they should not be extended.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband's acquisition of the woman should pull in all of her property.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the husband's control of new property is hard to explain, so old property stays the woman's and her sale is valid.
steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל's rule: we do not stretch the husband's rights over property that came to her before the relevant stage.

steps.title: Property inherited after marriage: the husband can take it back
steps.stepSummary: If she inherited after נישואין, both schools agree that if she sold it, the husband can take it back from the buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it came to her after she was married, both agree that if she sold it or gave it away, the husband takes it back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה reaches the third stage, after full marriage. Now the husband has real rights, so her sale does not hold against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After נישואין the husband gets rights to the use and produce of her property. A sale she makes would hurt those rights, so he can take the property back. This is the reverse of the outcome in Step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: After she was married (נישואין, full marriage)

phrases.english: If it fell to her after she was married,
both these and those agree
that if she sold or gave it away,
the husband takes it back from the hands of the buyers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the debate about the engagement stage, the משנה moves to the marriage stage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property inherited after נישואין: a sale by the woman can be cancelled by the husband, who takes it back from the buyers.

steps.title: Inherited before marriage, then married: רבן גמליאל says the sale stands
steps.stepSummary: If she got the property before נישואין and then married, רבן גמליאל rules that a sale she makes is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it came to her before she married and then she married, רבן גמליאל says: if she sold it or gave it away, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the in-between case. The property came to her before the wedding, but she sells it after the wedding. רבן גמליאל says the sale holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What decides the case is when the property came to her, not when she sold it. Since it was hers before the marriage, the husband's rights do not cancel her sale, even though she is married now.

keyTerms.meaning: Before she married, and then she married

phrases.english: If it fell to her before she married, and then she married,
Rabban Gamliel says:
if she sold or gave it away, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִשֵּׂאת וְנִשֵּׂאת, רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property she had before נישואין may still be sold after the marriage, and the sale is valid, according to רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: The same challenge again, this time about marriage
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן עקביא reports the same challenge, now aimed at the marriage case: since the husband acquired her, he should acquire her property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן עקביא said: they said before רבן גמליאל: Since he acquired the woman, should he not acquire the property?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same challenge, but here it is reported by a different תנא and is aimed at the case of full marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reporter tells the same exchange about a different stage. רבי יהודה tells it about אירוסין, and רבי חנינא בן עקביא tells it about נישואין. After marriage the challenge is even stronger, since the husband's tie to her is now complete.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hanina ben Akavya said:
They said before Rabban Gamliel:
Since he acquired the woman,
should he not acquire the property?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא, אָמְרוּ לִפְנֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge from Step 3, now applied to the marriage case in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's ruling that property she had before נישואין may be sold after it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Full marriage means the husband acquired her, so he should acquire her property as well.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל gives the same answer
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers the same way: the husband's rights to new property are already hard to explain, so they should not be stretched to old property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: We are embarrassed about the new property, and you want to pile the old property on us too?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל repeats his answer, now about the marriage case. Property she had before marriage stays hers to sell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same as in Step 4. Since the husband's control of after-marriage property is already hard to justify, it is not stretched to property from before the marriage.
steps.whatToRemember: Through all the stages, the deciding question is when the property came to her. Property from before a stage is not swept into the husband's rights from that stage.

phrases.english: He said to them:
About the new property we are ashamed,
and yet you roll the old property onto us?!

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the comparison by refusing to extend a rule that is already hard to explain.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marriage gives the husband all of her property.
steps.terutzMaskana: Property she had before marriage stays hers, and her sale is valid.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: property the husband knows about vs. property he does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון divides property into two kinds. She may not sell either one, but a sale of property the husband knows about is cancelled, while a sale of property he does not know about stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון makes a difference between one kind of property and another. Property the husband knows about: she may not sell it, and if she sold it or gave it away, the deal is void. Property the husband does not know about: she may not sell it, but if she sold it or gave it away, the deal is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a different way to look at the question. For him, what matters is whether the husband knew about the property, not when it came to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases she should not sell to begin with. The difference is only after the fact. If the husband knew about the property, he was counting on it, so her sale is cancelled. If he never knew about it, he was not relying on it, so the sale stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings in a new factor, what the husband knew and relied on, which differs from רבן גמליאל's focus on timing.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חוֹלֵק בֵּין נְכָסִים לִנְכָסִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon distinguishes between property and property:
property known to the husband: she may not sell it,
and if she sold or gave it away, it is void.
Property not known to the husband: she may not sell it,
but if she sold or gave it away, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חוֹלֵק בֵּין נְכָסִים לִנְכָסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different deciding factor (whether the husband knew) instead of when the property came to her.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property known to the husband: if she sells it, the sale is void. Property unknown to him: if she sells it, the sale is valid. In both cases she may not sell to begin with.

steps.title: Why do they agree in the first case but argue in the second?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the first case of the משנה different from the second, so that בית שמאי and בית הלל agree in one and argue in the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about the first part, where they do not argue, and what is different about the second part, where they do argue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking a basic question about the משנה. Why does the timing of the inheritance matter so much?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the woman holds the property now, after אירוסין. So why does it matter whether it came to her before or after אירוסין? The גמרא wants the reason behind the difference.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is different about the first part
phrases.notes: The first part is where she got the property before אירוסין.

phrases.english: that they do not argue,
and what is different about the later part
that they do argue?
phrases.notes: "They" means בית שמאי and בית הלל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה that was laid out in the earlier steps.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the timing of the inheritance, before or after אירוסין, decides whether בית שמאי and בית הלל argue.

steps.title: First case: her rights; second case: his rights
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי answer that in the first case the property came while she alone had rights, and in the second it came while he had rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: In the first part, it fell to her while the rights were hers. In the later part, it fell to her while the rights were his.
steps.whatsHappening: The students of רבי ינאי answer the question. Before אירוסין the inheritance came to her own rights, but after אירוסין it came to his rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that what counts is whose rights were in place when the property arrived. Before אירוסין the husband had no claim, so there is nothing to argue about. After אירוסין the husband already has rights, so there is room for a dispute.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
In the first part, it fell while the rights were hers.
In the later part, it fell while the rights were his.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whose rights were in place when the property came: hers before אירוסין, his after אירוסין.

steps.title: If the rights were his, why does her sale stand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: if property inherited after אירוסין came under his rights, why does בית הלל say her sale is valid?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it fell to her under his rights, then when she sold it or gave it away, why is the sale valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of דבי רבי ינאי. It points to a ruling in the משנה that does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even בית הלל, the stricter side, say that if she already sold or gave away the property, the sale stands. If the property truly came under the husband's rights, her sale should be cancelled. So the answer seems too strong.

keyTerms.meaning: She sold it or gave it away

phrases.english: If it fell under his rights,
when she sold it or gave it away,
why is it valid?
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה, where even בית הלל agree that a sale already made stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם בִּזְכוּתוֹ נָפְלוּ, כִּי מָכְרָה וְנָתְנָה אַמַּאי קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of דבי רבי ינאי that property inherited after אירוסין came under the husband's rights.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the husband truly had the rights, her sale would be cancelled. Yet the משנה rules that a sale already made is valid.

steps.title: After אירוסין, it is unclear whose rights came first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא refines the answer: before אירוסין the property was surely hers, but after אירוסין it is uncertain, so she should not sell, yet a sale already made stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: in the first part, it surely fell under her rights. In the later part, maybe it fell under her rights and maybe under his. So she should not sell from the start, but if she sold it or gave it away, the sale is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the answer of דבי רבי ינאי. After אירוסין it is a doubt whose rights the property came under.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new answer turns a definite claim (his rights) into an uncertainty (maybe hers, maybe his). Because of the doubt, she should not sell from the start. But a sale already made is not cancelled. This fits בית הלל's ruling exactly.
steps.whatToRemember: Before אירוסין the property is surely hers. After אירוסין it is a doubt. So according to בית הלל, she should not sell from the start, but a sale she already made stands.

phrases.english: Rather: in the first part,
it certainly fell under her rights.
In the later part, say it was under her rights,
or say it was under his rights.
From the start, she should not sell,
but if she sold it or gave it away, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by reworking the answer of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reworks the earlier answer: a certainty becomes a doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Property inherited after אירוסין definitely came under the husband's rights.
steps.terutzMaskana: After אירוסין it is a doubt whose rights came first, so she should not sell from the start, but a sale already made stands.

steps.title: Was רבי יהודה's report about selling from the start or after the fact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's line from the משנה and asks which ruling the Sages' challenge to רבן גמליאל was aimed at.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יהודה said, they said before רבן גמליאל. A question was asked: was רבי יהודה talking about selling from the start, or about a sale already done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and quotes it. Then it asks a new question about what that line refers to, setting up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages asked רבן גמליאל: since the husband acquired the woman, shouldn't he acquire her property too? The גמרא wants to know what this was aimed at. Was it aimed at בית שמאי's ruling that she may sell from the start? Or was it aimed even at the ruling that a sale already made stands, which בית הלל also accept?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
After the fact; once it was already done

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said,
they said before Rabban Gamliel.
A question was asked among them:
was Rabbi Yehuda talking about selling from the start,
or about a sale after the fact?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַלְּכַתְּחִלָּה, אוֹ אַדִּיעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first part of the משנה to רבי יהודה's report, and opens a new question about it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the Sages' challenge reported by רבי יהודה was aimed at selling from the start (בית שמאי) or at a sale already made (which בית הלל also accept).
